data_policy.statement: The kimi lane carries a no-household-personal-data routing constraint. It is approved for code and general technical work only; household personal data, personal correspondence, and identity-bearing content must never route to it.
data_policy.basis: Operating entity 北京月之暗面科技有限公司 (Beijing Moonshot AI); personal information stored within mainland China; training on inputs is the DEFAULT with only a contact-based opt-out; no GDPR/EEA language. Governing law differs between the two applicable agreements (Singapore for OpenPlatform, PRC for the assistant property) and no page states which binds a membership (audit U6) — the constraint is written to hold under either reading.
data_policy.enforcement_note: RECORDED AND SURFACED, NOT MACHINE-ENFORCED. No per-lane data-policy enforcement point exists in the tree as of 2026-08-24 (grep-verified at P3-LN-3); enforcement lands with the routing-policy seam, and this row is what that seam will read. overflow_note: overflow_mode is `opt-in-credits` on every model: the Extra Usage Credit Pack is OFF by default, requires funding, and carries an explicitly PROVEN disable (satisfying 3.10 / P-T17-2), verbatim: "You can turn it off at any time: your balance stays in your account and the system pauses spending from it; turn it back on to resume." RECOMMENDED OPERATOR POSTURE: Extra Usage OFF, under which the lane behaves as a hard stop and the ¥-denominated top-up rails are moot. Turning it on is a deliberate, reversible operator act through the rehearsed kill-switch operation — never automatic, never silent.

installed_catalogue_record.source: The provider record EMBEDDED in the npm-shipped opencode 1.18.3 platform binary — NOT a cached file. Corrected at drain r2 after this record's first cut was overturned by execution. opencode-ai@1.18.3 ships five platform binaries (bin/opencode.exe plus node_modules/opencode-linux-x64{,-baseline,-baseline-musl,-musl}/bin/opencode); `grep -ac "kimi-for-coding"` returns 3 on EVERY one of the five, and ~/.cache/opencode/bin is EMPTY. Read this round with a balanced-brace extraction over node_modules/opencode-linux-x64/bin/opencode. $0, local, no live provider call.
installed_catalogue_record.models_verbatim_note: The engine record's model ids, verbatim and complete: SIX. (An earlier report of a seventh id `crossmodel` did not reproduce — `'crossmodel' in record` is False on this host; it is not in this provider's record.) Each carries name/limit/reasoning_options; the ids above are what the engine will accept.
installed_catalogue_record.agrees: provider id `kimi-for-coding`; env var `KIMI_API_KEY`; npm `@ai-sdk/anthropic`; base URL `https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1`; and TWO of the four model ids this document declares — `k3` and `kimi-for-coding-highspeed`.
installed_catalogue_record.diverges: THREE divergences, each recorded rather than reconciled away. (1) `k3-256k` is ABSENT from the engine record — 0 occurrences across all five shipped binaries, not merely absent from one. (2) `kimi-for-coding` is the PROVIDER KEY, never a model id: the engine's model ids are the six listed above. (3) The name `Kimi For Coding` is the PROVIDER's display name; `Kimi K2.7 Code` is model `k2p7`'s name. This record's first cut conflated (3) and attributed real 262,144 context limits to the two ids in (1) and (2), which do not exist in the engine record — that conflation is removed and the limits are re-attributed below.
installed_catalogue_record.limits: Attributed to the ids that actually carry them: `k3` context 1,048,576 / output 131,072; `k2p5`, `k2p7`, `kimi-k2-thinking`, `kimi-for-coding-highspeed` and `k2p6` context 262,144 / output 32,768. Every model is priced $0.00 in the record — the S03.7 corollary, so this lane's dollars come from Sinet's own metered rows and NEVER from the engine.
installed_catalogue_record.reasoning_options: `k3` declares reasoning_options `[{type:"toggle"},{type:"effort",values:["max"]}]`. TWO consequences, both dated 2026-08-24. (a) The engine record's effort vocabulary for k3 is `["max"]` ALONE, which corroborates this document's unverified-primary grading of the brief-sourced `["low","high","max"]`. (b) A `toggle` type EXISTS, which contradicts this document's claim that Kimi publishes no thinking disable and that the Z.AI `thinking:{type:disabled}` lever has no equivalent — that claim is therefore also graded unverified-primary and left unwired. Nothing is built on either; the ceremony and the account's observed list decide.
installed_catalogue_record.second_source_disagrees: A DIFFERENT record exists on this host and disagrees: a runtime-fetched models.dev snapshot written by a real `opencode serve` at 2026-08-23 19:45 into a per-user XDG cache (models.json, 4.3 MB) lists this provider's models as `k3`, `k3-256k`, `kimi-for-coding`, `kimi-for-coding-highspeed`. That file is where this record's first cut came from, and reading it as 'the installed engine's record' was the error. Recorded as a dated fact rather than resolved: two sources disagree, the engine binary is what this pinned version will accept, and NEITHER is the authority over the ACCOUNT — which is exactly what the model-list canary exists to settle (P-T17-3).
installed_catalogue_record.note: The engine record is a SEED like everything else here. It is authoritative over documentation for what this pinned engine accepts, and still not authoritative over the account's observed model list.
